title: A computer-certified closeness bound for the Kummer K3 surface of the Hurwitz lattice
description:
In plain words. A K3 surface is a four-dimensional shape that carries a perfectly balanced geometry, a Ricci-flat metric, which exists by Yau's theorem but has no formula. The Kummer construction gets close by hand: fold a flat four-dimensional torus in half and smooth its 16 corner points with small Eguchi-Hanson bubbles of size a. Since 1990 it has been known that the perfect geometry is close to the glued one if a is small enough; how small and how close was never computed. We computed both and proved them with interval arithmetic.

Result. For the Kummer K3 surface of the Hurwitz (D4) lattice and an explicit approximant omega_a, we prove with interval-arithmetic computer assistance that (1+d)^-1 omega_a ≤ omega_CY ≤ (1-d)^-1 omega_a for every bubble size a in (0, 0.03], with d(0.01) ≤ 2.851e-3, d(0.03) ≤ 0.121974, d(a)/a^3 ≤ 2275.00 for a in (0, 1e-4] and limsup d(a)/a^3 ≤ 2269.27. a0 = 0.03 is where the certificate stops (the proved range of the diameter lemma), not a limit of the method.

Credit. The qualitative estimate is due to Kobayashi (1990), re-proved by Lye (2023) and improved in weighted norms by Jiang (2025); the Green-operator representation and the leading Green-sum structure are due to Fu, Liu, Xiao and Yau (arXiv:2610.11077; Correction 2026-11-17: author list updated), who state that a certified a0 remained open. An explicit-interval bound proved by hand exists for a Schoen Calabi-Yau threefold (Fu, Liu, Xiao and Yau, arXiv:2610.21932). Certified Calabi-Yau metrics on the Fermat quartic are due to Douglas, Gómez-Serrano, Lehmann, Platt and Qi (arXiv:2611.16908) and Liu and Zhang (arXiv:2611.15319).

Conditions and checks. Conditional on a floating-point layer assumption (IEEE outward rounding in parts of three runs) and standard facts listed in the paper. Clean-room rebuild identical; all three load-bearing pieces (assembly, bulk residual peak, full core) replicated by blind independent code; nine hostile referee reports; algebraic steps checked in Lean. Every sealed test is listed: 8 HOLD, 3 FAILED, 4 VOID.

Open doors. The bound stops at bubble size 0.03 because of our diameter lemma, not the method; a sharper lemma could extend it, which we did not attempt. We found no explicit constants (search of 2026-11-17) for nearby K3 metrics with unequal bubbles or a deformed torus; keeping the bubbles aligned, as our method requires, leaves 28 of the 58 directions of the K3 moduli space. The other 30, where each bubble tilts its own way, need a new linear step for hyperkähler triples; Jiang (2025) proved this family exists, with qualitative constants. The same assembly should apply to other Kummer-type gluings with an explicit bubble metric, which we did not try.

Prepared with AI assistance; what was checked, and by what, is stated above.
